title: Keep common spool header keys inline
question: Can fixed-size keys avoid transient heap admission without changing framing or ownership?
summary: Inline eight/sixteen-byte decode keys preserve framing and ownership; the scoped native pipeline pairs favor the change.

workloads: One million probe-v1 pipeline rows, four workers, 32-MiB job/shared limits.

validation.summary: Six jobs preserve fields, IDs, groups, caps, CSV/Analysis parity and cleanup. Fixed/truncated/variable-key ownership controls and recorded premeasurement workflows pass.

limitations: Small development cells and uncontrolled cache/background state do not establish general device, shape or tail performance.
Historical percentage gains are not additive; every comparison uses its own pinned baseline.
Larger Head descriptors and non-fixed keys retain their own capacity costs; no lower whole-Run peak or RSS bound follows.
exclusions: Ordered control does not establish an improvement.
Failed Clippy and superseded workflow attempts remain failures, not additional observations.
